lesson.title: PHP 8: The Consolidation Continues
lesson.summary: Understand php 8 the consolidation continues from first principles, with a small runnable example.

stage.name: Orientation: why design matters
stage.subtitle: Book chapters 1–2
stage.description: Why projects fail, the accidental success of PHP objects, and how the book is organised.

payload.markdown: PHP has always been a great magpie, borrowing shiny proven features from other languages. PHP 8 introduces many new features including attributes, often known in other languages as annotations. These handy tags can be used to provide additional contextual information about classes, methods, properties, and constants in a system. Furthermore, PHP 8 has continued to extend its support for type declarations. Particularly interesting in this area is the union type declaration. This allows you to declare that the type of a property or parameter should be constrained to one of several specified types. You can lock down your types at the same time as taking advantage of PHP’s type flexibility. The very definition of having your cake and eating it!

items: Attributes: Structured metadata attached to classes and members, readable at runtime.
Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Constants: Immutable named values declared with const or define().
Properties & Methods: Class state held in properties, and behaviour implemented as methods.
Type Declarations: Parameter and return types that constrain what a function accepts and returns.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Constructor Property Promotion: Declaring constructor parameters as properties in a single step (PHP 8).
Dynamic Properties: Creating properties by assignment instead of declaration; deprecated since PHP 8.
